newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras rises on telcom law, market up.
newsitem.headline: Telebras rises on telcom law, market up.

text.p: Shares of Telebras shot higher after a local news agency published a summary of a bill creating Brazil's new telecommunications law, brokers said.

The rise boosted the broader Sao Paulo bourse in the early afternoon. Telebras preferred was up 1.01 percent at 80.30 reais, while its voting common surged 2.2 percent to 69.70 reais after the leaked summary was reported.
"It means that the matter is coming out, that something is happening with the law, that it will be voted on," a dealer told Reuters.
On the wider bolsa, the Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares rose 0.98 percent to 68,019 points by 1400 local time/1100 EST.

The bolsa's rise was due partly to Telebras, which regularly comprises 60 percent of total daily trade in Sao Paulo, and partly as a result of comments by officials that bolsa trade should be exempt from the new CPMF tax on financial transactions.
"That 0.2 percent tax means we could lose business," a broker said.
Meanwhile, the telecom law is expected to go to Congress's lower house this week, but officials at Congress and the Communications Ministry denied they had released any summary of the bill.
Agencia Estado, which published an eight-page summary of the bill, said it received the document from market sources, but did not elaborate.

Market analysts and traders who read the Estado report said it did not appear to contain any real market-moving revelations and stock prices were simply reacting emotionally to apparent progress on the law.
The new General Telecommunications Law is expected to create a general framework for the sector and a regulatory agency, and outline the government's plans to privatize the Telebras system.
